headline: US stocks rallied as easing oil prices and lower Treasury yields lifted risk assets and AI optimism boosted tech ahead of the Trump–Xi summit
raw_text:
- The Nasdaq Composite ($COMP) climbed 2.26% to a record 27,122.09, the S&P 500 ($SPX) rose 1.49% to 7,764.22, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average ($DJI) gained 0.72% to 52,053.88, with nine of 11 S&P 500 ($SPX) sectors closing higher.
- Communication Services led sector gains, rising 4.2% as Meta Platforms (META) jumped 6.2% after Wells Fargo raised its price target following the launch of the Muse AI assistant and related momentum.
- Information Technology advanced 2.4% as Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) surged 8.5% to reach a $1 trillion market capitalization amid renewed AI spending optimism and reports of progress in US–China AI talks ahead of a Trump–Xi summit, while Intel (INTC) and Arm Holdings (ARM) also rallied on AI enthusiasm.
- Consumer Discretionary gained 1.8%, while Energy fell 2.0% as West Texas Intermediate crude (@CL) dropped more than 3% to an 11-day low on hopes for US–Iran and broader Middle East diplomatic progress at this week’s UN meeting.
- Accenture (ACN) climbed 3.5% after announcing a $2 billion partnership with Anthropic focused on AI model evaluation.
- Critical Metals (CRML) soared 35% after President Trump announced a Greenland security agreement with Denmark.
- Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) jumped more than 10% and Paramount Global (PSKY) advanced after Paramount settled state antitrust lawsuits, including with California, clearing a major hurdle toward their planned $110 billion merger, with both stocks extending the move in extended trading.
- Novo Nordisk (NVO) fell 7.9% after CEO Mike Doustdar outlined 2030 goals that lacked the new blockbuster details investors had been anticipating.
- Treasury yields retreated even as Fed Governor Adriana Musalem said strong demand and inflation pressures may require further rate hikes, reinforcing expectations following last week’s Fed move.
- After the bell, Ennis Inc. (EBF) reported Q4 EPS of $0.38 versus $0.39 expected, while muted after-hours reactions to earnings from ABIVAX (ABVX) and AnaptysBio (ANAB) left index futures little changed as investors look ahead to the Trump–Xi summit, upcoming housing data, and additional earnings.
